full_judgment:
KM Hasan J: The Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner Chittagong to show cause why the order dated 17.10.93 passed by the Sessions Judge and Senior Special Tribunal Chittagong in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3534 of 1993 rejecting the application of the petitioner to transfer the Special Tribunal Case No. 12/93 pending in the Second Court of Assistant Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal Sadar Chittagong to the Juvenile court at Tongi, Gazipur should not be set aside or such other or further order of orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that the petitioner along with three others was apprehended by police on 16.3.1992 at about 8-15 PM with an eleven inches long pipe gun and one cartridge. The police after investigation submitted charge-sheet against the petitioner and his eldest brother, under section 19(a) and (f) of the Arms Act, 1978 on 25.5.1992. The petitioner moved an application on 17.10.93 being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3534 of 1993 before the Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal, Chittagong for transfer of Special Tribunal Case No. 12/93 to the Juvenile Court at Tongi Gazipur. But the learned Senior Special Tribunal and Sessions Judge Chittagong rejected the application by his order dated 17.10.93. Being aggrieved by that order the petitioner moved this application and obtained this Rule. 

 3. Mr. Alimuzzaman Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that at the time when the offence was committed the petitioner was less than sixteen years of age. In fact, he was 14 years 4 months and 20 days, his admit card for SSC examination, a Certificate from Noapara Muslim High School and a birth certificate issued by the Chairman of the union parishad (all annexed) show that the petitioner was born on 26.10.77 and the offence was committed on 16.3.92. Therefore the case comes under the purview of the Children Act 1974 and ought to be dealt with and disposed of by the Juvenile Court established at Tongi, Gazipur. 

 5. But in the instant case the petitioner was not sent to any institute of approved home or committed to anyone's custody to stop the passage of time for the purpose of computing his age. 

 8. In this case we also find that the petitioner is charge sheeted along with an adult. So the first task before the court is to determine the age of the petitioner under section 66 of the Children Act which is to the effect: 

 "66(1) Whenever a person whether charged with an offence or not, is brought before any criminal court otherwise than for the purpose of giving evidence, and it appears to the court that he is a child the court shall make an inquiry as to the age of that person and for that purpose shall take such evidence as may be forthcoming at the hearing of the cases, and shall record a finding thereon stating his age as nearly as may be." 

 In view of the above, the Rule is made absolute and the case is sent back on remand to determine the age of the accused petitioner on the basis of section 66(1) of the Children Act, 1974 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3534 of 1993 and send the accused petitioner to the juvenile Court if he has found below 16 at the time of framing of the charge. If he is found 16 years of age the trial Court will proceed with Special Tribunal Case No. 12/93 and dispose it of accordingly. The accused petitioner will remain on bail till the disposal of the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3534 of 1993.
